text:
Testing plays a vital role in software development. Unit tests check individual functions or components in isolation, ensuring each piece works correctly on its own. Integration tests, on the other hand, verify that different parts of the system work together smoothly, catching problems that might only appear when components interact.

Many developers practice test-driven development, or TDD, where they write tests before the actual code. This approach may seem backwards at first, but it helps clarify what the code should do. Ultimately, a solid testing strategy builds confidence. Knowing that automated tests cover common scenarios allows developers to make changes and add new features without constantly worrying about breaking something that already worked.
